sections.h2: Where to file and who to call
sections.html:
Walk into the courthouse at 101 Main Street in Oxford (NC 27565) or phone 919-693-6314. Mail can go to P.O. Box 427.

The counter opens weekdays at 8:30 AM and closes at 5 PM. Anything ordered online after 4 PM is handled the following business day. Ring ahead for a sale and ask what staff will want to see for your instrument, since they do not draft or repair documents.

The register is an elected countywide officer, serving a two-year term under G.S. 161-1.

Land records make up the bulk of the work, including deeds, deeds of trust, cancellations, plats, assumed names and powers of attorney. Every item is recorded, indexed and scanned, and the deed books go back to 1746.

  • Land records: deeds, deeds of trust, plats and cancellations.
  • Personal records: births, deaths, marriages and marriage licenses.
  • Other filings: military discharges and notary commissions, plus the oath for Granville County notaries.

Think of it as a recording counter rather than a legal clinic. Because state law bars the office from practicing law, staff cannot give you legal forms, walk you through completing one, or interpret a recorded document. Take those questions to a North Carolina attorney.

sections.h2: Fees when a deed is filed
sections.html:
Two charges show up on most sales. One is the recording fee, identical statewide under G.S. 161-10. The other is the seller's excise tax.

Granville County recording charges
DocumentRecording fee
General instrument$26.00 for pages 1 to 15, plus $4.00 per page after
Mortgage or deed of trust$64.00 for pages 1 to 35, plus $4.00 per page after
Cancellation of a deed of trustNo charge
Excise tax, paid by seller$1.00 per $500 of value, remainder rounded up

The transferor owes the tax under G.S. 105-228.30, and it must be paid before the deed is recorded. Half goes to the county. A tract lying in several counties pays in whichever holds the most value. Since the amount comes from the price stated in the deed, check that the deed matches your actual contract before signing.

A deed that never gets recorded cannot be enforced against later buyers or lien creditors. G.S. 47-18 hands priority to whichever instrument is registered first, measured by time, where the land is located.

Leases longer than three years, options and rights of first refusal follow the same rule. If you are carrying the financing yourself, Chapter 47H applies: the contract or a Memorandum of a Contract for Deed should be recorded inside five business days, and the buyer may cancel until midnight of the third business day.

The office offers a free alert tool called PropertyCheck. Owners can sign up for an email or text whenever a document is recorded that matches a name, a street address or a parcel number.

  • Register on the vendor's website.
  • Create alerts for each version of your name and for your spouse.
  • Add the property address and parcel number.

The fraud in question works like this: a forger transfers title to a different name and records the papers while the true owner knows nothing. An alert cannot stop a filing. What it gives you is time to phone 919-693-6314 and reach a lawyer fast.

sections.h2: Vital records at the Oxford counter
sections.html:
Certified birth, marriage and death certificates cost $10.00 apiece, and plain copies cost $1.00. Orders placed online carry a $4 service and card fee that is not refundable. The system holds records from 1913 forward, and each request must include a copy of valid photo ID.

Newlyweds should wait 10 days after the ceremony before ordering a certified marriage copy. To collect a record in person, bring valid state-issued photo ID. Collecting for someone else is restricted to these people.

  • The person named on the record.
  • A spouse, brother or sister, parent or step-parent, grandparent, or child, step-child or grandchild.
  • A funeral director, for a death certificate only, with proof of license.
  • An authorized agent, attorney or legal representative, who may be asked for proof.

Online requests are served in order received, refunds are not offered, and updates on an order come by email.

sections.h2: What to check in the records before closing
sections.html:
Begin by searching your own parcel in the online records. With documents viewable online and copies available on request, you can pull your vesting deed and old loan papers from home.

  • The deed that put the property in your name, with matching spelling and legal description.
  • Any deed of trust that was paid off but never cancelled of record.
  • Plats or easements that affect the parcel.
  • Assumed-name filings, if a business ran from the house.

Fixing problems before you list beats fixing them under a closing deadline. When a recorded instrument looks wrong, ring 919-693-6314 to learn how it can be corrected, and hire an attorney for anything requiring legal drafting.

sections.h2: The recording counter and the tax office
sections.html:
Two offices, one subject. The recording counter moves title. Granville County Tax Administration (919-693-4181) sets values and bills the tax. A balance owed becomes a lien on your parcel dating to the January 1 listing date (G.S. 105-355), so plan to clear it before the new deed goes on record.

A 1.5% discount applies to current taxes paid from July 1 through August 15, with the bill due September 1. Closing in that window? Ask the tax office what paying promptly would save. Whether the land is in Oxford, Butner, Creedmoor, Stem or Stovall, the deed is filed at the one Oxford courthouse counter.

Granville County has 25,685 housing units and 22,474 households, averaging 2.52 residents each. Building permits in 2025 numbered 257, and the midpoint monthly cost for owners with a mortgage is $1,546. Recording charges come from state law, so they stay the same whatever those numbers do. Local market figures matter for pricing, not for what the Oxford counter charges to file.

Here is a workable order for a seller. First, look up your parcel online and ask the tax office for a written balance. Second, gather payoff letters and confirm that old loans were cancelled of record. Third, have your attorney prepare the deed, because the register's staff cannot. Fourth, on closing day, the seller's excise tax is paid before filing, and the deed is recorded in Oxford. Last, keep copies of the recorded deed and the tax receipt.

A cash sale skips the lender's paperwork and appraisal. It does not skip the recording or the tax, and the buyer's attorney will still search the same records you searched. If something surfaces, such as an old uncancelled deed of trust, fixing it early keeps the closing date from slipping.

faqs.q: What will a standard deed cost to file?
faqs.a: Filing runs $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 per page beyond that under G.S. 161-10. On top of that, the seller pays excise tax of $1.00 per $500 of value.
Monday through Friday, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM. If your deed is out of the ordinary, ring 919-693-6314 before you drive over.

faqs.q: Can staff prepare my deed for me?
faqs.a: No. North Carolina law keeps recording staff from practicing law, so they cannot supply forms or advise on legal effect. Hire an attorney for drafting.

faqs.q: Is a loan payoff cancellation free to record?
faqs.a: Yes. The state fee schedule has no charge for a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust or mortgage.

faqs.q: How far back do Granville deeds go?
faqs.a: Deeds are available back to 1746, while vital records ordered online start in 1913.
